findings.mechanism: Connection pool default size (5) may be exhausted under load, limiting concurrency. Cites 02-connection-pooling-and-pool-exhaustion.
findings.remediation: Configure SQLAlchemy engine with a larger pool_size (e.g., pool_size=10) to exceed expected concurrent requests per worker.
findings.arithmetic: Workers=4 (Dockerfile). Default DB pool size=5. Assuming DB latency 100ms, each worker can handle 10 rps, total 40 rps. At load 80 rps, each worker's pool fully utilized (5 connections). Active connections per worker reach 5.

findings.mechanism: No statement timeout on DB queries allows a slow or hanging DB to block workers indefinitely. Cites 03-timeouts-as-a-first-principle.
findings.remediation: Set a statement timeout (e.g., asyncpg timeout=5s) via SQLAlchemy execution_options or database configuration.
findings.arithmetic: Workers=4. Each ready request holds one worker and one DB connection. With no timeout, a DB latency of 30s keeps the worker blocked. Four concurrent hanging requests saturate all workers: worker_saturation=1.
